validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE / CLASSIFICATION / DUPLICATE all clear. This is Texas Eastern Transmission Company's (TETCO, an Enbridge/Spectra Energy Partners subsidiary) real, FERC-certificated 'Access South Project' -- FERC Docket CP16-3-000 (Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity issued Dec 21, 2016, filed jointly with the Adair Southwest and Lebanon Extension projects; pre-filed under PF15-17-000 June 2015; formal application Oct 8, 2015). Confirmed by THREE mutually independent sources: (1) TETCO/Spectra Energy Partners' own project page (archived, spectraenergypartners.com, since the live enbridge.com successor 404s) -- Peak Day Capacity 320,000 Dth/d, Completion Date November 2017, Ownership 100% Texas Eastern Transmission LP, footprint states PA/WV/OH/KY/TN/AL/MS; (2) Rice Energy Inc.'s SEC 8-K (filed 2014-11-12, an unrelated shipper, not Enbridge-affiliated) -- table lists 'Access South TETCO Nov-17 320,000 25 Yrs Gulf Coast'; (3) Vantage Energy Inc.'s SEC S-1 (2016, a second, separate, unrelated shipper) -- lists 'Texas Eastern Transmission Company Access South Project 320 Q4 2017' in its pipeline-capacity-additions table alongside the separate 200 MMcf/d 'Adair Southwest Project' (confirming Access South and Adair Southwest are genuinely distinct projects with different capacities, not this row's duplicate -- neither Adair Southwest nor Lebanon Extension appears elsewhere in this 46-row roster, so no merge action here). Correctly classified: interstate FERC-jurisdictional gas transmission expansion, Gas commodity, operating status confirmed by all three (in-service Nov 2017, no shutdown/abandonment evidence found, consistent with LastUpdated 2023-08-21). Opened and read to exhaustion: the Spectra project page, Rice Energy 8-K exhibit, Vantage Energy S-1 exhibit, Enbridge's 2017 SEC 6-K annual report (via BankTrack-hosted PDF, Wayback-verified), and the harvested FracTracker/NGI/SEC citations already on the wiki page (NGI article is subscriber-paywalled even via Wayback -- headline only, cannot read body; FracTracker page is a generic multi-pipeline map that never names 'Access South' in text, so it is not usable as a corroborating ref -- name_found false). Owner1=Enbridge (100%, ultimate parent convention) and the newly-filled Operator=Texas Eastern Transmission LP (the actual FERC-jurisdictional operating subsidiary) do not conflict -- see the Operator/Owner fills.

validity.recommendation: sharply reduce LengthKnown -- current 1287 km appears to record the Uniontown,PA-to-Kosciusko,MS mainline distance, not the pipe actually built; verify against the FERC CP16-3-000 order/EA before pasting any replacement number
validity.researcher_notes: MATERIAL SPEC DISAGREEMENT. GEM records LengthKnown=1287.00 km (~800 route-miles), which is roughly the highway/mainline distance between the recorded termini Uniontown, PA and Kosciusko, MS. But TETCO's OWN project page -- the same page that supplies the capacity and in-service-date values above -- describes the actual constructed facilities in one explicit sentence: 'Facilities Shared facilities with Access South and Lebanon Extension: 16 miles of pipeline relay or loop within or adjacent to existing Texas Eastern ROW; Additional compression at existing stations; 3 existing receipt meters converted for bi-directional flow; Various other modifications to existing facilities.' Enbridge's own 2017 SEC 6-K annual report corroborates the SCOPE (not the mileage): 'The facilities for these projects include pipeline looping, as well as modifications and expansions of existing compressor stations on SEP's Texas Eastern pipeline system' -- i.e. this is a looping/compression expansion of an EXISTING mainline corridor, not ~800 miles of new pipe. 16 miles (~25.7 km) is the combined figure for Access South AND Lebanon Extension together, so Access South's own share is some unknown fraction of that -- meaning the true value is almost certainly under 26 km, not 1287 km, an overstatement on the order of 50x. This is the exact 'route/corridor distance vs actual new pipe' confusion the sweep SOP warns about (c.f. Rockies Express Zone 3 in this same roster). I am NOT proposing a specific replacement number because the 16-mile figure is not disaggregated between Access South and Lebanon Extension and I found no second, independent source stating a mileage (FERC eLibrary's docket-sheet UI is a JS single-page app that returns no content to scripted fetches -- CP16-3-000 needs a browser session to pull the actual order/EA PDF, which would very likely state exact looping mileage by segment; the NGI article naming this docket is subscriber-paywalled even via Wayback; SEC full-text search for other shipper filings turned up only capacity/timing, no mileage). Do not paste 0 either -- some new pipe clearly was built, just not 800 miles of it.
